answer: Continuous identity beacon fee curve: each identity must emit a recurring beacon pulse, priced by a convex curve over how many pulses share a registration root. A grove of linked identities pays a marginal cost that rises with sibling count, so the N+1th pulse costs progressively more than the previous. An attacker minting N identities at one source pays roughly quadratic total cost while honest single identities pay a flat base fee, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. A fable of cheap identities becomes expensive fast.
